newsitem.title: USA: CME hogs seen steady-lower, pork bellies steady-up.
newsitem.headline: CME hogs seen steady-lower, pork bellies steady-up.

text.p: CME hog futures were expected to open steady to 0.100 cent per lb lower while pork belly futures were called steady to 0.200 cent a lb higher, livestock analysts said.
Cutting of slaughter hours by at least one major meat packer should keep pressure on hog futures as it cuts demand for cash hogs and pushes live prices lower, some sources said.
IBP Inc said Monday it would cut back on production at its hog slaughter plants due to tight hog supplies.
However, support may develop on the Japanese announcement that that country will exempting some pork imports from tariffs in August.
Japan Agriculture Ministry said it will exempt some pork imports from tariffs as a way to lower pork prices in Japan.

Most analysts anticipate strength in nearby pork belly futures on the reduced hog slaughter indications. Packers cutting kills will reduce the amount of bellies entering the marketing pipeline, analysts said.
However, some analysts look for resistance in belly futures as values need to invert. Frozen values are above fresh and need to move under fresh prices to encourage seasonal withdrawals.
Analysts' estimates on the weekly CME out-of-town report ranged from a net out-movement of 2.8 million to 3.2 million lbs versus 2.914 million lbs out last week and 3.402 million lbs out last year.
